value.rationale: The physically natural joint weak-shear/rare-excursion scaling retains longitudinal Brownian fluctuations at order one in the large-deviation rate, unlike the random-acceleration approximation. The new boundary measures when one observable rare endpoint is preferentially generated by a short or long elapsed time since resetting; the explicit strictly positive thermal shift gives a quantitative, testable distinction and a two-component conditional-age law. This is not a freely chosen finite numerical cutoff.
